analysis_steps.goal: Reduce IRDIS polarimetric data to Q_phi images

method.value: IRDAP alignment, bad pixel correction, sky background subtraction, then polarimetric differential imaging; median-combined Q_phi with stellar polarization removed, default parameters

evidence.quote: `IRDAP` performs alignment, bad pixel correction, and sky background subtraction.
By adopting the default `IRDAP` reduction parameters, we use median-combined output $\mathcal{Q}_\phi$ images with stellar polarization removed for spiral motion analysis

analysis_steps.goal: Rescale images by r^2 to correct for stellar illumination

method.value: Multiply Q_phi images by an r^2 map normalized at 0.5 arcsec

evidence.quote: we rescaled the brightnesses of the $\mathcal{Q}_\phi$ images by multiplying them with a $r^2$ map
to obtain the $r^2$-scaled maps (normalized at $0\hbox{$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$}5$)

key_parameters.value: inclination 16.7 deg from face-on, position angle 61.9 deg

evidence.quote: assuming a $16\hbox{$.\!\!^\circ$}7$ inclination from face-on and a $61\hbox{$.\!\!^\circ$}9$ position angle for the major axis of the disk (cite: bohn22)

assumptions.value: Infinitely thin disk because of the low inclination

evidence.quote: Given the low disk inclination, we assumed an infinitely thin disk for subsequent analysis

analysis_steps.goal: Measure spiral peak radii at each azimuth and epoch

method.value: Transform r^2-scaled maps to polar coordinates; at each angle fit a normal distribution to the radial profile to get the peak and its error

evidence.quote: For each angular location, which is defined as a clockwise separation from the major axis of the disk, we fit a normal distribution to obtain the peak and its associated error on the spiral radial profile.
With a $1^\circ$ angular step, we present the peaks and their errors

fitting.value: Normal (Gaussian) distribution fit per angular location; sampler/priors not stated

evidence.quote: we fit a normal distribution to obtain the peak and its associated error on the spiral radial profile

analysis_steps.goal: Fit spiral morphology and pattern motion across epochs

method.value: Fit an identical polynomial to each arm at the three epochs with an angular offset per epoch via dummy variables; best-fit offset is the angular rotation between epochs; fit uncertainty propagated with true north and astrometric uncertainties

evidence.quote: we followed Ref. (cite: ren20) to fit an identical but angularly offset polynomial
the best-fit offset will be the angular rotation among the epochs

the polynomial fitting uncertainty will be propagated with three epochs of $0\hbox{$.\!\!^\circ$}08$ SPHERE true north pointing uncertainty in Ref. (cite: maire16) and three epochs of SPHERE astrometric uncertainty of $0\hbox{$.\!\!^\circ$}16$.

key_parameters.value: p-degree polynomial in angle theta; degrees used 6, 7 and 8 (arm and fit dependent); astrometric uncertainty 0.16 deg in polar coordinates

evidence.quote: The astrometric accuracy of SPHERE/IRDIS is $\sim$2 mas ($\sim$0.16 pixels; (cite: Zurlo2014)), thus translating into $0\hbox{$.\!\!^\circ$}16$ in polar coordinates.

fitting.value: Polynomial with dummy-variable epoch offsets; reduced chi-squared reported; sampler, priors and likelihood not stated

claims.result: S1 -0.84 +/- 0.05 and S2 -0.87 +/- 0.05 deg/yr, consistent within 1 sigma; combined -0.85 +/- 0.05 deg/yr
claims.finding: The spirals are consistent with a single driver

evidence.quote: The spiral motions of S1 and S2 are consistent within $1\sigma$, suggesting that they are driven by a single driver.

claims.hypothesis: The spiral rotation rate locates the hidden driver, which may also carve the ALMA dust gap
claims.experiment: Convert omega to a circular orbit for a 1.6 Msun star and compare with ALMA dust continuum gap and filament
claims.finding: The predicted orbit is consistent with the disk gap and coincides with the filament

evidence.quote: For a $1.6\pm0.1M_\odot$ star and assuming a circular orbit, the obtained $\omega = -0\hbox{$.\!\!^\circ$}85\pm0\hbox{$.\!\!^\circ$}05~{\rm yr}^{-1}$ rotation rate corresponds to a hidden planet at $66\pm3$ au

why_this_data.value: Same band (J) at three epochs to get the longest high-quality baseline and avoid wavelength-dependent spurious motion

evidence.quote: To establish the longest temporal separation of high-quality data for analysis, and reduce the possibility that wavelength-dependent imaging manifests spurious spiral motion

why_this_method.value: Spiral motion tracking dynamically tests spiral formation mechanisms

evidence.quote: tracking the motion of the spirals can dynamically test leading spiral formation mechanisms

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gravitational instability not tested again because the earlier 1-yr study ruled it out

evidence.quote: since it has been confidently ruled out with the study on $1$-yr separation for SAO 206462 (cite: xie21)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Two independent planets would sit at 69 au and 62 au, close together but not in low-order resonance, which is taken as consistent with the single-driver scenario

evidence.quote: While the two planets are mathematically close to each other, they are not under low order mean motion resonance

limitations_admitted.value: Fits assume independent azimuthal angles; correlation among adjacent pixels is not accounted for

evidence.quote: thus it is necessary to take into account the correlation among adjacent pixels.

limitations_admitted.value: The predicted protoplanet is not detected

evidence.quote: While this protoplanet is currently not detected

referee_caveats_inferred: Reduced chi-squared of 1.8 to 3.5 indicates the polynomial error model is not fully adequate, so quoted 0.05 deg/yr uncertainties may be underestimated
The ALMA data play only a qualitative comparison role; no ALMA processing, imaging or measurements are reported
Circular-orbit and thin-disk assumptions drive the 66 au radius; eccentric orbits are not explored

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA imaging details and the exact image used in the orbit overlay figure
Angular ranges and masks for the spiral peak fits
Fitting algorithm, priors and chi-squared definition
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small: three SPHERE/IRDIS DPI datasets (ESO archive, likely a few GB); no ALMA reprocessing needed
reproducibility.score_reason: Numeric results are given, but the paper does not state data availability, gives no code, and defers key method choices to earlier papers; the ALMA component is only an overlay.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public availability of the SPHERE data is not stated, fitting details are incomplete, and the ALMA part is not reproducible from the paper.
